ai.literal: The strength of the action, and one's own strength, and the strength of the adversary, and the strength of the ally, having weighed, act.
ai.translation: Weigh well the strength of the deed, your own strength, the strength of your adversary, and the strength of your allies, and then act.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயலைச் செய்வதற்கு முன், அச்செயலின் வலிமை, தன் வலிமை, பகைவனின் வலிமை, மற்றும் துணையாக இருப்பவரின் வலிமை ஆகியவற்றை ஆராய்ந்து பார்த்து அச்செயலைச் செய்ய வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the four essential types of strength that must be evaluated before embarking on any major undertaking. First, one must understand the difficulty of the task itself (vinai vali). Second, one must assess their own capabilities and resources (tan vali). Third, the power of the opponent or obstacles must be gauged (māṟṟāṉ vali). Fourth, the strength of one's supporters or allies must be factored in (tuṇai vali). Only after carefully weighing (tūkki) these four elements should one proceed to act (ceyal).

words.gloss: that which is to be known

ai.literal: Knowing what is possible, knowing what is to be known, abiding in that, to those who proceed, that which is impossible does not exist.
ai.translation: For those who understand what is possible for them, learn what needs to be known about the task, and proceed while abiding within those limits, there is nothing that is impossible to achieve.
ai.modern: தனக்கு இயன்றதையும், அறிய வேண்டியவற்றையும் அறிந்து, அந்த எல்லைக்குள் நின்று செயல்படுபவர்களுக்கு முடியாதது என்று எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the secret to achieving any goal without failure. First, one must assess their own capability ('ஒல்வது') and thoroughly understand the requirements and obstacles of the task ('அறிவது'). Second, they must act while strictly staying within the limits of this realistic assessment ('அதன்கண் தங்கி'). For those who proceed with such careful planning and self-awareness, there is absolutely nothing that remains impossible ('செல்லாதது இல்') to accomplish.

ai.literal: Their own strength not knowing, by mere enthusiasm spurred on, in the middle broke down many.
ai.translation: Many are those who, not knowing the measure of their own strength, are spurred on by mere enthusiasm and break down midway.
ai.modern: தங்கள் சொந்த வலிமையை அறியாமல், வெறும் ஆர்வத்தினால் மட்டும் தூண்டப்பட்டுச் செயலில் இறங்கி, வழியிலேயே அழிந்துபோனவர்கள் பலர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against starting an enterprise based solely on passion without assessing one's actual capability. 'உடைத்தம் வலி' refers to one's own strength or resources, which must be measured realistically. 'ஊக்கம்' means zeal or enthusiasm, which is a powerful motivator but dangerous when blind. Those who act out of mere excitement without self-evaluation are described as 'இடைக்கண் முரிந்தார்'—they break down and fail halfway through their journey.

words.gloss: he who does not conduct himself

ai.literal: Having adapted in that manner not conducting himself, the measure not knowing, himself exalting, quickly will perish.
ai.translation: One who does not live in harmony with others, does not know the measure of his own strength, yet exalts himself, will quickly be ruined.
ai.modern: மற்றவர்களுடன் பொருந்தி வாழாமல், தன் வலிமையின் அளவையும் அறியாமல், தன்னைத்தானே வியந்து பாராட்டிக் கொள்பவன் விரைவாக அழிவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against the dangers of self-conceit combined with ignorance of one's actual strength and a failure to cooperate with others. The word 'அமைந்து' (amaintu) here means adapting or living in harmony with one's surroundings and associates. 'அளவு அறியான்' (aḷavu aṟiyāṉ) refers to a person who does not assess their own capabilities, resources, or limitations. When such a person additionally 'வியந்தான்' (viyantāṉ)—meaning they self-exalt or hold an inflated opinion of themselves—they lose all sense of reality. Consequently, their downfall ('கெடும்') is not just certain, but will happen very rapidly ('விரைந்து').

ai.literal: Peacock-feather-loaded cart-even axle-will-break that-cargo greatly exceeding if-loaded.
ai.translation: Even the axle of a cart loaded with light peacock feathers will break, if that cargo is loaded in great excess.
ai.modern: மயில் தோகையை ஏற்றிய வண்டியாக இருந்தாலும், அந்தப் பண்டத்தை அளவுக்கு அதிகமாக ஏற்றினால் வண்டியின் அச்சும் முறிந்து போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid metaphor to explain the danger of accumulation and the importance of knowing limits. Peacock feathers are incredibly light individually, but when loaded onto a cart in extreme excess, their cumulative weight will snap the strong wooden axle. Similarly, even minor challenges, small enemies, or seemingly insignificant tasks can overwhelm and destroy a person if they are allowed to accumulate beyond measure.

words.gloss: if they attempt to go further

ai.literal: Those who climbed the tip of a branch, if they attempt to go beyond that, it will end up becoming the end of their life.
ai.translation: If those who have climbed to the very tip of a tree branch attempt to push further beyond that limit, it will result in the end of their life.
ai.modern: மரக்கிளையின் நுனிவரை ஏறியவர்கள், அந்த எல்லையையும் தாண்டி மேலே செல்ல முயன்றால், அது அவர்களுடைய உயிருக்கே முடிவாகிவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid physical metaphor to warn against overreaching one's limits. A climber who has already reached the absolute tip of a branch is at the peak of danger; if they try to push even further, the branch will break, leading to a fatal fall. In the context of acting according to one's strength, it teaches that exceeding the absolute limit of one's capacity, even after achieving great heights, brings total ruin. The word 'ookkin' here refers to the foolish attempt to exert oneself beyond the safe boundary, which inevitably ends in disaster.

ai.literal: According to one's means, properly knowing, give; that is the way of preserving and distributing wealth.
ai.translation: Give to others according to your means, knowing the proper way; that is the path to preserve and distribute your wealth.
ai.modern: ஒருவர் தன் வருவாயின் அளவுக்கு ஏற்ப, அறநெறியை அறிந்து பிறருக்குக் கொடுக்க வேண்டும்; அதுவே செல்வத்தைப் பாதுகாத்து வழங்கும் வழியாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the importance of giving within one's capacity. The word 'āṟṟiṉ' means according to one's ability or financial means, emphasizing that charity should not exceed what one can afford. 'Aṟa aṟintu' means knowing the proper, virtuous way of giving. The poet explains that giving in this balanced, mindful manner is actually the true path to both preserving and distributing one's wealth without destroying oneself.

ai.literal: Even if the measure of the incoming path is small, there is no ruin, if the outgoing path does not widen.
ai.translation: Even if the source of income is small in measure, there is no ruin as long as the path of expenditure does not exceed it.
ai.modern: வருமானம் வரும் வழி சிறியதாக இருந்தாலும், செலவு செய்யும் வழி விரிவடையாமல் இருந்தால் அழிவு இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the fundamental principle of financial management. The poet uses the terms 'āgāṟu' (the incoming path or income) and 'pōgāṟu' (the outgoing path or expenditure) to describe a person's budget. Even if one's income is very small ('iṭṭitu'), there will be no ruin ('kēṭu illai') as long as the expenses do not expand ('agalā') beyond that limit. The conditional word 'kaṭai' (if) emphasizes that financial survival depends entirely on keeping expenditure within the bounds of income.

words.gloss: he who does not live accordingly

ai.literal: Knowing the measure, he who does not live, his life, as if existing, becoming non-existent, without appearing, will perish.
ai.translation: The life of one who does not live knowing the measure of his resources will seem to prosper, but will vanish without a trace and perish.
ai.modern: தன் பொருளின் அளவை அறிந்து வாழாதவனுடைய வாழ்க்கை, இருப்பது போலத் தோன்றி, பின் இல்லாமல் போய், சுவடு தெரியாமல் அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against living beyond one's means. The word 'அளவு' refers to the limit or measure of one's wealth and resources. If a person does not live ('வாழாதான்') with this awareness, their prosperity ('வாழ்க்கை') might outwardly look abundant and real ('உள போல'). However, this illusion of wealth will quickly turn into nothing ('இல்லாகி') and disappear so completely that even the trace of its former existence will not be seen ('தோன்றாக் கெடும்').

words.gloss: the limit of what one possesses

ai.literal: The limit of what exists without estimating, the practice of benevolence, the limit of wealth quickly will be ruined.
ai.translation: The practice of benevolence without estimating the measure of one's own resources will quickly ruin the limits of one's wealth.
ai.modern: தனக்கு இருக்கும் பொருளின் அளவை ஆராய்ந்து பார்க்காமல் பிறருக்கு உதவி செய்யும் தன்மையானது, ஒருவனுடைய செல்வத்தின் எல்லையை விரைவாக அழித்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against blind or disproportionate generosity. While helping others is a noble duty, practicing benevolence without first assessing the limits of one's own resources leads to financial disaster. The poet emphasizes that even substantial wealth has its limits, and unsustainable giving will quickly deplete those resources. Therefore, charity must always be balanced with realistic self-awareness of one's financial strength.
